summary: At 104ff465 the v2 declarative JSON compiler accepts only the protocol, swap and credit domains. Funding is a separate strict plugin domain: it has defineFundingFamily, its own capability-slot table and a separate funding runtime, but there is no declarative-funding compiler, no funding module catalogue and no JSON-to-FundingFamilyPlugin path. The only production JSON format that currently accepts production.domain='funding' is bindings-v1, which merely imports the existing TypeScript morphoFlashManifest/morphoFlashDiscovery/morphoFlashFunding/morphoFlashFamilyOwnedAction objects; it declares no semantics and is not a declarative cutover. Therefore a faithful declarative Funding JSON cannot be authored under the no-public-TS/no-tests constraint. The handwritten listener/src/searcher/venues/production-families/morpho-flash.production.ts remains authoritative.

existingSource.fact: renderDataFamilyEntry casts production.domain to protocol|swap|credit, throws 'unsupported declarative v2 domain' otherwise, and maps the constructor suffix with swap/credit/else-Protocol (funding falls through to Protocol).
createDeclarativeFamilyRuntime rejects any version-2 definition whose production.domain is not protocol, swap or credit: 'unsupported declarative Family version/domain'.

The v2 renderer resolves the compiler as src/searcher/venues/declarative-${domain}.ts and imports compileDeclarative${Suffix}; no listener/src/searcher/venues/declarative-funding.ts exists at 104ff465 (git ls-tree), so the funding path has no compiler at all.

FAMILY_CAPABILITY_APPLICABILITY.funding allows only manifest (required), capture (optional), discovery (required), actionAdapters (required) and funding (required); identity, instance, routes, pricing, exact, execution and sharedBindings are 'never'.
The v2 schema requires version, scope, production, manifest, discovery, identity, instance, routes, pricing, the domain block, standard, actionAdapters and variantFiles.

The compiled definition always emits discovery, identity, instance, routes, pricing, exact and execution plus the domain block; that object shape cannot be passed to defineFundingFamily, whose table forbids those slots.

The v2 optional-module catalogue contains liveStateProjection, instanceEvidence, executionProjection, pricingProjection, quoteOutput, signedBlockEvidence, oracleVictim, math, executionMath, quoteFlow, pricingFlow and trialState only; there is no funding liquidity/read/offer/repayment module.

defineFundingFamily is only a thin defineFamily wrapper. validateFamilyPlugin branches on expectedDomain==='funding', validates discovery and validateFundingDomain, and never treats a data document as a plugin; it is not a JSON compiler.

Authored design statement: Funding still has its own domain interface, but the current v2 JSON compiler accepts only the three routed domains (Protocol/Swap/Credit); Funding must not be inferred to be JSON-ified.

decisiveBlocker.frameworkLimitation: The v2 data-JSON schema, runtime and production renderer are routed-family contracts. Funding has an independent strict plugin contract consumed by adapter-funding-runtime and the solver; it has discovery plus funding semantics but no identity/instance/routes/pricing/exact/execution slots. Adding a faithful Funding JSON would require a public framework extension, not a JSON-only migration. Relaxing the one domain check would still fail: the renderer would emit compileDeclarativeProtocol/defineProtocolFamily shape, and defineFundingFamily would reject the extra route slots.

secondaryBlockers.fact: The v1 path accepts domain=funding and renders format=bindings-v1 by importing every manifest/discovery/funding/action binding from relative TypeScript modules (probe C). It adds JSON indirection around the existing TS family, not JSON declaration of its semantics; generating the entry would require the generator and a TS production entry, both outside this task.

createErc20BalanceFundingSemantics derives one source per observed asset (200-220), builds a per-asset balanceOf(liquidityHolder) request program (221-257), derives fee-0/maxBorrow offers (258-279), and builds approve-pull repayment plus the nested borrow fragment (281-310). flash-loan-framework.ts:60-230 is the legacy duplicate of the same dynamic shell. No JSON module catalog block can declare these functions.

The Morpho action is isWrapper:true with field2Offset=100, encodes flashLoan(address,uint256,bytes) and embeds the inner script as the bytes argument so Morpho can callback onMorphoFlashLoan. The declarative action compiler hardcodes isWrapper:false and field2Offset:null (listener/src/searcher/venues/declarative-execution.ts:1057). A JSON action declaration therefore cannot replace the wrapper action; only binding the existing TS action adapter preserves it.

The build-time scan only looks for <name>-family/<name>.json beside a *-family directory and feeds it to renderDeclarativeProductionEntry. listener/src/searcher/venues/funding/morpho-flash-family/ contains only TS files (no morpho-flash.json); adding one would reach the v2 domain rejection at 118. The active entry remains the handwritten production-families/morpho-flash.production.ts (generated-production-family-entries.generated.ts imports entry28 at lines 30 and 81).

nonBlockingAnalysis.note: These are structural observations, not an implementation or acceptance claim.
expressibleIfAFundingSchemaExisted: Discovery: the FlashLoan(address,address,uint256) topic, singleton emitter MORPHO, indexed token topic 2 and providerFromBlock 0 are data-shaped and could be declared; the existing discovery types already model logPatterns and singleton-indexed-address.
Liquidity: one source per observed asset, target/liquidityHolder both MORPHO, fee 0, maxBorrow from balanceOf(MORPHO), planningPriority 0 and liquidityPriority 1 are simple data/pure derivation.

Repayment: approve-pull is a static erc20-approve fragment with MAX_UINT spender=MORPHO and minimumAllowance=amount; the borrow fragment is morpho-flash with children assert-balance then erc20-approve.

Registration: manifest domain funding, ownedActionAdapterIds ['morpho-flash'], requiredInfraActionAdapterIds ['assert-balance','erc20-approve'], allowedTaxonomy [{slotKind:'flash'}], supportedLineages ['morpho-flash'] and the env key are all data.
nonBlockingAnalysis.missingContract: What does not exist is a funding-domain JSON contract and compiler that turns those facts into the FundingDomainSemantics functions and a FamilyOwnedActionAdapter (including the wrapper/callback action). Until that exists, any JSON is either rejected (v2) or a pure TypeScript binding manifest (v1).

unblockRequirement: A public framework change is required before any faithful flash-loan:morpho Funding JSON can exist: (1) admit domain='funding' in the v2 data-family runtime and production renderer; (2) add a declarative-funding compiler that emits the FundingFamilyPlugin shape (manifest, optional capture, discovery, funding semantics and actionAdapters) without importing TypeScript implementation; (3) add funding module catalogue blocks for dynamic per-asset sources, current-N read program, pure offer derivation, repayment and borrow fragments; (4) preserve or declare the Morpho wrapper action (isWrapper/field2Offset=100 and the onMorphoFlashLoan callback) or keep binding the existing action adapter; (5) register/load the generated funding entry and extend the funding tests plus build:live. This is out of scope for the JSON-only, no-public-TS task.
nextSteps: Keep listener/src/searcher/venues/production-families/morpho-flash.production.ts and the funding TS modules unchanged.
Do not author a v1 bindings-only 'JSON cutover': it would not migrate semantics and would still need the generator plus a TypeScript entry.
Do not narrow the family to a route-shaped Protocol/Swap/Credit JSON; such a definition would fail the funding plugin contract and would not preserve funding discovery/liquidity/repayment behavior.
If the framework later gains a funding-domain JSON compiler and wrapper-action declaration, re-run this assessment and then author the JSON under the normal migration validation.
